column1: # The time budget of every job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, in minutes from the
# job's start to its end (time in the queue does not count).
# The job "CI job time budgets" runs scripts/ci-job-budgets.py on its own run.
# It warns when a job took longer than its budget, and it fails when a job that
# runs on pull requests ("pr") took longer than 20 minutes, the project's rule,
# or a nightly job longer than its budget. It is not a required check, so a
# slow runner cannot block a merge, and a broken rule still shows in red. A
# pull-request job's budget may be at most 17 minutes, which leaves three
# minutes of margin before the rule. scripts/ci-job-budgets_test.sh checks that
# every job has exactly one budget and that each fits under the job's
# Each budget is about 1.3 times the slowest of ten runs on 12 November 2026
# (five on main, five pull requests), within the ceiling. The two Native Go
# 1.27.3 jobs were one job then (21 to 22 minutes); their budgets come from that
# job's step times and the first run of the split. Nightly jobs have their
# timeout-minutes as their budget. Raise a budget only in the pull request that
# makes the job slower, and say why in that pull request.
# Columns, separated by tabs: minutes, scope (pr or nightly), the job's name as
# GitHub shows it, with * in place of a matrix value.
